questions.prompt: With a good hash function and bounded load factor, what is the average time of a hash-table lookup — and its worst case?

options.text: O(log n) average, O(n) worst case
O(n) average, O(n log n) worst case

questions.explanation: Even distribution keeps buckets tiny (O(1) average), but if every key collides into one bucket you scan all n entries (O(n) worst case).

questions.prompt: The load factor of a hash table is defined as...

options.text: n / m — entries divided by buckets
m / n — buckets divided by entries
the length of the longest chain
the number of hash collisions so far

questions.explanation: Load factor α = n/m measures fullness; as it grows, collisions increase, which is why tables resize to keep α bounded.

questions.prompt: Which statements about hash tables are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Chaining stores colliding entries in a per-bucket list
Open addressing probes for another open slot on a collision
Python dict and set keys must be hashable
Hash-table lookup is guaranteed O(1) in the worst case

questions.explanation: Chaining and open addressing are the two collision strategies, and keys must be hashable. The O(1) is an average, not a worst-case guarantee.

questions.prompt: The two main collision-resolution strategies are chaining and ______ addressing. (one word)
questions.explanation: Open addressing keeps all entries in the bucket array and probes for the next available slot when a collision occurs.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a hash-table lookup (chaining).

items.text: Reduce it to a bucket index (mod m)
Compare stored keys for equality and return the match

questions.explanation: Hash the key, map it to a bucket, scan that bucket's short chain, and compare keys to find the entry.

questions.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.

pairs.right: Bucket holds a list of colliding entries
Probe for another slot on collision
Recompute buckets for all entries on resize

questions.explanation: These are the core hash-table concepts: fullness ratio, the two collision strategies, and the resize operation.
